newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Investor says Saab loss narrows.
newsitem.headline: Investor says Saab loss narrows.

text.p: Swedish investment company Investor AB said losses in its Saab unit narrowed to 97 million crowns in the first quarter versus 132 million in Q1 1996.
Saab AB, which is a fully-owned subsidiary of Investor, makes high-tech products for aerospace and defense.

It said invoices for the group rose 13 percent to 2.31 billion crowns in the first three months of the year. The increase was attributed to invoices for six JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets compared to three in the same 1996 period.

The group's order bookings for the first quarter amounted to 1.83 billion crowns compared to 2.68 billion in the same 1996 period. The order backlog amounted to 19.75 billion crowns compared to 21.54 billion at the end of the period.
